project.title: Vara — ideal product graph
project.goal: Turn spoken intent into useful, trustworthy text in the user’s working context, with explicit control over meaning, processing and recovery across desktop platforms.
project.scope: First release: approachable setup and everyday dictation delivering faithful text with optional light cleanup into the intended app, with safe cancellation and recovery. Build modularly with clear GDD contracts. File transcription, AI answers and wake word are deferred. Direct transcription is the default; optional AI cleanup/adjustment uses general or app-specific editable system prompts. App-specific prompts are included; explicit per-app enablement runs AI automatically with that app’s prompt. Other apps use direct transcription by default; processed output follows the same focus-safe automatic delivery without extra approval. Technology, platform release matrix and detailed quality budgets remain open. Target macOS, Windows and Linux in the first release, with Mac-first development and final Windows/Linux verification. Rust is the working technical direction; the UI toolkit and exact supported environments remain open. Support both local and explicitly chosen cloud processing; local is the default for the first-use workflow. Save completed results in Vara grouped by the originating app, with focus-safe automatic insertion and clipboard preservation. Direct cloud API access uses personal API keys with easy in-app configuration; optional installed CLI text adapters may use their own user authentication. A Vara-managed cloud/login/billing service is outside this scope. Initial provider baseline follows existing cloud integrations, Ollama and own OpenAI-compatible text endpoints behind extensible GDD contracts; local model choice remains under evaluation. Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI are included as optional text adapters; subscription speech is a research candidate, not a verified release feature. Start with an empty profile; importing previous Vara data/settings is excluded. Keep product decisions focused and refine technical details only when needed.
assumptions: Mikkel is the primary first-release user. Other users must be able to get started without technical setup. The first-release workflow is everyday faithful dictation with optional light cleanup, safe delivery, cancellation and recovery.
Accepted first-release membership is recorded separately in vara.release_scope. Remaining core/next/explore labels are discussion priorities, not automatic release promises.
The previous Swift implementation provides experience, not required structure or automatic feature parity.
All product nodes are sketches. This graph is a planning deliverable, not implementation evidence.
Development and ongoing runtime testing take place on macOS. Windows/Linux runtime testing is deferred until the final verification phase; their support is not considered verified before that phase.

Local processing is the default for audio and optional text cleanup. Cloud is a deliberate user preference, never an automatic setup/failure fallback. Cloud uses user-supplied provider keys, with provider-specific costs handled externally; no Vara login/billing service is planned.

Cleanup/rewriting is optional. Unprocessed dictation skips generative text processing. The default mode is direct transcription without extra text AI. When processing occurs, persist both original and processed text; show the finished text first with the original accessible.

action.retention.label: Control history and recovery retention
action.retention.description: Control whether text/audio persists and when it is deleted.

vara.accepted_constraints: Text history: retain until manual deletion by default; optional automatic cleanup after a user-selected period. Audio retention is still open.

postconditions: Clearly distinguish text history, temporary recovery audio and diagnostics; enforce the selected retention without implying secure erasure guarantees that are not established.

By default retain text history until the user deletes it, without an implicit age or item-count cap. Only an explicitly enabled automatic-cleanup setting applies a user-chosen retention period. Text history and audio retention are distinct policies.
Deleting or expiring a history result covers both its original and processed text where both exist; do not leave the original as hidden retained history.
Successful-transcription audio is deleted regardless of text-history lifetime. Failed-transcription audio is retained only temporarily for retry, with a distinct expiry; it is not a history item.

Failed-transcription audio has a fixed maximum 24-hour recovery lifetime, deleted earlier on successful retry or explicit user deletion. Retry attempts do not extend the original expiry. Expired input cannot be reused; purge it at expiry while running and on next startup/resume if execution was suspended. Report cleanup failures instead of claiming deletion succeeded.

Expected outcome: Clearly distinguish text history, temporary recovery audio and diagnostics; enforce the selected retention without implying secure erasure guarantees that are not established.

Default text-history expiration is disabled. Let users enable timed cleanup and choose its period; explain the effect of a changed setting. Never silently apply a legacy history item cap. Audio policy and raw-versus-final persistence are separately specified.
For failed audio, assign a fixed 24-hour expiry when first retained. Delete earlier after successful recognition or explicit deletion. On startup/resume and before retry, enforce expiry and clean orphaned recovery captures. A suspended/nonrunning app cannot perform physical deletion; do not present expired audio as recoverable.

rule.cancellation.label: Cancellation prevents late effects

rule.destination.label: Do not guess a destination
rule.destination.description: A changed or uncertain destination must not receive automatic insertion; retain the text and offer a deliberate next step.

rule.statement: Automatically insert only into the original text target while its focus is unchanged. Changed or uncertain focus, including a different field in the same app, leaves text available for deliberate manual insertion. Save the result under the originating app regardless of its later delivery destination.

rule.fallback.label: Keep raw text on AI failure
rule.fallback.description: Optional AI failure or timeout must leave raw text usable and label which processing failed.

rule.statement: Optional AI failure or timeout must leave raw text usable and label which processing failed.

rule.locality.label: No hidden network fallback
rule.locality.description: Only-on-this-device policy constrains both audio and text, including retries, CLI tools and fallback engines.

rule.statement: Local processing is the default for speech and optional text cleanup. Cloud requires an explicit user choice with clear audio/text destinations. Local setup or processing failure does not authorize upload. Strict only-on-this-device policy continues to constrain retries, subprocesses and fallback engines.

rule.retention.label: Retention is explicit
rule.retention.description: Recovery audio and text history obey distinct visible settings; when retention is disabled, do not promise later recovery.

rule.statement: Text history is retained until the user deletes it by default, with no hidden time/count truncation. Timed automatic cleanup is optional and uses the user-selected period. Recovery audio, diagnostics and text history have separate visible policies; do not infer indefinite audio retention or promise recovery after input deletion. Delete audio after successful transcription, even if later cleanup/delivery fails. Temporarily retain failed-transcription audio for retry under a separate expiry policy; successful retries delete that audio. Text history contains no audio attachments. Failed audio expires at a fixed 24-hour maximum and is deleted earlier after successful retry or explicit deletion. Repeated failures do not reset that deadline. Reject expired recovery and clean it on startup/resume if the application was not running; report physical deletion failures.

rule.no_content_logs.label: Diagnostics exclude content by default

rule.approachable_setup.label: Start without technical setup
rule.approachable_setup.description: Mikkel is the primary user, while other users can complete first use without becoming engine or infrastructure administrators.

rule.statement: Provide an approachable local first-use path without terminal commands, manual endpoints, API keys or a Vara account. Explain necessary permissions and model downloads. Optional cloud processing uses user-supplied provider keys through a clear in-app flow; keep provider-specific details discoverable when that route is chosen. No Vara-managed login/billing cloud service is in scope.

rule.module_contracts.label: Explicit GDD module contracts
rule.module_contracts.description: Changes and extensions use explicit responsibility boundaries and public contracts. Concrete modules are specified before their implementation.

rule.statement: Before implementing a module, declare its responsibility, exclusions and public actions in GDD. Specify relevant inputs, outputs, errors, effects and failure/cancellation guarantees, with scenarios. Consumers use the owning provider’s public contract; contract changes identify affected consumers and scenarios. Apply this to actual required modules, not speculative layers.

scenario.local_default.label: Local first use with optional cloud
scenario.local_default.description: Planned check of the accepted default; not an executed application test.

scenario.given: A fresh installation has no processing preference or configured cloud service.
scenario.when: The user follows setup and performs a first dictation, then inspects the alternative processing choice.
scenario.then: Local speech and local optional cleanup are the default. Required assets are explained and set up through the app. Cloud is discoverable but sends no speech/text until the user explicitly chooses and configures the allowed route.

action.configure_shortcut.label: Choose activation mode and shortcut
action.configure_shortcut.description: Choose a personal global shortcut and either hold-to-talk or toggle behavior, with hold-to-talk as the default.

errors.ShortcutUnavailable: Explain the OS limitation or conflict and retain the last working assignment.

postconditions: The user can choose and test a supported shortcut and activation style. Hold-to-talk is the initial default. Persist a successful choice; an unsuccessful assignment leaves the previous working choice intact.

action.configure_shortcut.behavior:
User trigger: Choose an activation mode, record a shortcut and test it in settings.
Expected outcome: A supported user-selected shortcut activates the selected style; failures are actionable and preserve the last working configuration.
Exact OS binding, effect and error contracts remain to be specified.

scenario.hold_default.label: Hold-to-talk default
scenario.hold_default.description: Planned activation example; not an executed test.

scenario.given: A first-use profile has a supported configured shortcut.
scenario.when: Press and hold, speak, then release.
scenario.then: Begin capture once on key down and stop for transcription on matching release; no toggle-mode setup is required.

scenario.toggle_selected.label: Toggle mode is selectable
scenario.toggle_selected.description: Planned activation example; not an executed test.

scenario.given: The user has selected toggle mode.
scenario.when: Press the configured shortcut, speak, then press it again.
scenario.then: Start once, ignore key repeat as an extra press, and stop once on the second deliberate activation.

scenario.shortcut_conflict.label: Unsupported shortcut preserves setup
scenario.shortcut_conflict.description: Planned activation example; not an executed test.

scenario.given: A working shortcut exists and a new chosen binding cannot be registered.
scenario.when: Save the new shortcut.
scenario.then: Explain the limitation/conflict and preserve the previous working binding.

rule.clipboard_preservation.label: Preserve clipboard during automatic delivery
rule.clipboard_preservation.description: Automatic delivery must preserve clipboard contents and respect concurrent user copying.

rule.statement: Automatic insertion must preserve preexisting clipboard content and applicable formats. Restore temporary paste state only while it is still owned by this operation; never overwrite a newer user copy. If preservation cannot be assured, retain text for manual use. Explicit user Copy is an intentional clipboard change.

scenario.history_origin.label: History follows originating app
scenario.history_origin.description: Planned delivery/history example; not an executed application test.

scenario.given: Dictation starts in app A and the user switches to app B while processing.
scenario.when: Processing completes.
scenario.then: Skip automatic insertion, retain the completed result in Vara grouped under A, and make manual use available.

scenario.same_app_new_field.label: Same app but different field
scenario.same_app_new_field.description: Planned delivery/history example; not an executed application test.

scenario.given: Dictation started in text field X and focus moves to field Y within the same app.
scenario.when: Text becomes ready.
scenario.then: Do not automatically paste into Y; retain the result for deliberate use under the original app.

scenario.clipboard_preserved.label: Existing clipboard survives insertion
scenario.clipboard_preserved.description: Planned delivery/history example; not an executed application test.

scenario.given: The clipboard contains preexisting content in applicable formats and the original target remains focused.
scenario.when: Automatically insert a completed result.
scenario.then: Deliver the text while preserving prior clipboard content and formats.

scenario.clipboard_concurrent_copy.label: Concurrent user copy wins
scenario.clipboard_concurrent_copy.description: Planned delivery/history example; not an executed application test.

scenario.given: Automatic paste temporarily owns the clipboard and the user copies new content before cleanup.
scenario.when: The paste operation attempts restoration.
scenario.then: Do not restore old content over the newer user copy.

scenario.history_until_deleted.label: History has no default expiry
scenario.history_until_deleted.description: Planned text-retention example; no persistence implementation tested.

scenario.given: History has its default retention setting and contains old entries.
scenario.when: Time passes and more dictations are completed.
scenario.then: Do not remove saved text because of age or an implicit item cap; manual deletion still works.

scenario.history_timed_cleanup.label: Optional timed cleanup
scenario.history_timed_cleanup.description: Planned text-retention example; no persistence implementation tested.

scenario.given: The user has deliberately enabled automatic cleanup with a chosen period.
scenario.when: An entry reaches the configured expiry.
scenario.then: Apply the selected text retention policy, leaving newer entries intact and not changing the separate audio policy.

scenario.raw_skips_processing.label: Unprocessed dictation skips text AI
scenario.raw_skips_processing.description: Planned check of the explicit optional-processing clarification.

scenario.given: The user selects unprocessed dictation.
scenario.when: Speech recognition finishes.
scenario.then: Deliver and save the transcript under the originating app without calling a cleanup/rewriting model. Show one text result; do not invent a processed duplicate.

scenario.processed_history_versions.label: Inspect original of a processed result
scenario.processed_history_versions.description: Planned text-history example; no application execution claimed.

scenario.given: A completed dictation was processed and saved under its originating app.
scenario.when: The user opens the saved result and chooses to inspect the original.
scenario.then: Display the finished text first and allow access to the unchanged original transcript. Both versions belong to that result and follow its deletion/expiry policy.

scenario.successful_audio_deleted.label: Successful audio is deleted
scenario.successful_audio_deleted.description: Planned audio-policy check; not executed application behavior.

scenario.given: A dictation’s speech recognition succeeds.
scenario.when: Optional cleanup or delivery subsequently fails.
scenario.then: Keep usable text and delete audio; do not retain audio because of a later text/delivery error.

scenario.failed_audio_retry.label: Failed audio is temporary retry input
scenario.failed_audio_retry.description: Planned audio-policy check; not executed application behavior.

scenario.given: Speech recognition fails and available audio is temporarily retained.
scenario.when: The user retries within the allowed lifetime and recognition succeeds.
scenario.then: Reuse the capture, delete it after recognition succeeds, and save text only in originating-app history.

scenario.audio_expiry_deadline.label: Failed audio reaches expiry
scenario.audio_expiry_deadline.description: Planned expiry/deletion example; not an executed application test.

scenario.given: Failed-transcription audio has a fixed 24-hour expiry.
scenario.when: The deadline is reached and the user tries to retry.
scenario.then: Reject use of expired input and delete it while running; show recovery expired, without extending the deadline.

scenario.audio_expiry_restart.label: Restart after failed-audio expiry
scenario.audio_expiry_restart.description: Planned expiry/deletion example; not an executed application test.

scenario.given: The application was stopped/suspended while recovery audio passed its deadline.
scenario.when: The application starts or resumes.
scenario.then: Purge expired/orphaned recovery audio before offering retry. Do not claim physical cleanup ran while the app was stopped.

scenario.audio_manual_delete.label: User deletes recovery audio
scenario.audio_manual_delete.description: Planned expiry/deletion example; not an executed application test.

scenario.given: A failed capture is still within its recovery lifetime.
scenario.when: The user explicitly deletes it.
scenario.then: Delete it immediately while running and remove its retry option; do not wait for the 24-hour deadline.

entity.system_prompt.label: Editable system prompt
entity.system_prompt.description: User-controlled AI cleanup/adjustment instructions, general or assigned to an originating application. Separate prompt configuration from activation and processing locality.

scenario.raw_initial_default.label: Fresh profile uses direct transcription
scenario.raw_initial_default.description: Planned default/prompt example; no app execution claimed.

scenario.given: A new profile has not opted into AI text processing.
scenario.when: The user completes a dictation.
scenario.then: Deliver the speech-model transcript without optional text AI; save one text representation.

scenario.general_system_prompt.label: Optional general prompt processing
scenario.general_system_prompt.description: Planned default/prompt example; no app execution claimed.

scenario.given: The user deliberately selects AI processing using a configured general system prompt.
scenario.when: The transcript is sent to the selected allowed text engine.
scenario.then: Use those visible instructions, honor local/cloud policy, save original and processed text, and show processed text first.

scenario.app_system_prompt.label: Prompt follows invocation app
scenario.app_system_prompt.description: Planned default/prompt example; no app execution claimed.

scenario.given: A system prompt is assigned to app A and dictation starts there.
scenario.when: The user changes foreground app while the dictation is processed.
scenario.then: Keep A as prompt-selection context; changing focus does not switch the prompt or authorize automatic insertion. AI activation follows a separately specified choice.

entity.app_processing_settings.label: Per-app AI setting
entity.app_processing_settings.description: Explicit app-to-prompt activation preference; distinct from prompt content and from permission to send text to cloud.

scenario.app_ai_enabled.label: Enabled app automatically processes
scenario.app_ai_enabled.description: Planned per-app activation check; no application execution claimed.

scenario.given: The user enabled AI processing for app A with prompt P.
scenario.when: Dictation is invoked in A and recognition completes.
scenario.then: Automatically process with P under the allowed local/cloud policy; retain A’s processing context if foreground focus changes.

scenario.app_ai_not_enabled.label: Other apps remain direct
scenario.app_ai_not_enabled.description: Planned per-app activation check; no application execution claimed.

scenario.given: The user is in app B without an enabled AI preference; a general or app prompt may exist.
scenario.when: Dictation in B finishes recognition.
scenario.then: Use direct transcription without optional text AI by default; prompt existence alone does not enable it.

scenario.ai_ordinary_delivery.label: AI result inserts without extra approval
scenario.ai_ordinary_delivery.description: Planned check of accepted AI delivery; not executed application behavior.

scenario.given: AI processing completed using an explicitly selected or app-enabled prompt.
scenario.when: The finished result reaches delivery.
scenario.then: If the original text target still has focus, automatically insert without extra approval and preserve the clipboard. Otherwise keep the result ready for manual insertion. Save original and finished text under the originating app.

scenario.cloud_personal_key.label: Configure a personal cloud key
scenario.cloud_personal_key.description: Planned BYOK setup check; no live provider/credential operation executed.

scenario.given: Local default works and the user deliberately chooses a supported cloud provider.
scenario.when: The user adds a personal API key through the app.
scenario.then: Store it appropriately, expose actual credential readiness and enable only the authorized cloud route; require no Vara login or payment account.

scenario.cloud_rejected_key.label: Rejected key is actionable and private
scenario.cloud_rejected_key.description: Planned BYOK setup check; no live provider/credential operation executed.

scenario.given: The user submits an invalid or rejected provider key.
scenario.when: Credential validation or the requested provider operation fails.
scenario.then: Explain the provider/key issue without logging the secret; retain local functionality and do not report cloud as ready.

rule.provider_contracts.label: Extensible provider contracts
rule.provider_contracts.description: Provider integration stays behind explicit speech/text contracts so additional providers can be added without changing unrelated user flows.

rule.statement: Define GDD contracts for speech recognition and optional text processing: accepted audio/transcript/system-prompt input, outputs, capabilities, actual processing locality, readiness, credential needs, errors, cancellation/timeouts and external effects. Keep protocol/endpoint details in the owning provider adapter. A new provider fulfills those contracts and scenarios without rewriting capture, delivery or history. Do not require speculative dynamic plugins or promise capabilities an endpoint does not support.

scenario.custom_text_endpoint.label: Configure an own text endpoint
scenario.custom_text_endpoint.description: Planned custom-endpoint example; no endpoint requests executed.

scenario.given: The user chooses a compatible custom text endpoint and its declared locality is allowed by the processing policy.
scenario.when: The user configures URL/model and any required personal API key, then explicitly uses AI processing.
scenario.then: Use the same text-processing contract and original/finished history behavior as other providers; keep secrets in appropriate storage and report actual readiness/protocol errors.

action.cli_processing.label: Use an optional installed CLI for text AI
action.cli_processing.description: Use Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI as an optional text-processing provider through its own installed/authenticated tool and an explicit provider contract.

annotations.vara.locality: A locally launched CLI may send content remotely; classify actual processing, not process location.

errors.ToolUnavailable: Explain missing executable or unusable authentication without extracting tokens.
errors.ToolFailed: Keep the original transcript available and report a redacted error.

postconditions: Offer the three CLI text routes only as optional integrations with actual tool/readiness detection. Use the tool’s own authentication; do not require a Vara subscription or copy login tokens.

Apply the configured system prompt and return only the intended text result through the same history/delivery contracts. Respect actual network locality, cancellation and timeout; failure preserves raw text.

action.cli_processing.behavior:
User trigger: Explicitly choose an installed Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI text provider.
Expected outcome: Use its genuine executable and own authentication for bounded transcript processing, without changing user-global CLI settings or treating the subprocess as automatically local inference.
Fully specify permissions, isolation, capability/auth detection, output parsing and cancellation before implementation. Voice capability is separately researched.

question.audience.statement: Who is the primary first-release user, and which daily task matters most?

question.release_scope.statement: For Mikkel first, with approachable setup for others, which core/next/explore proposals belong in the first release and which daily workflows matter most?

question.platforms.statement: Which OS versions, Linux desktop environments, hardware and capability fallbacks will we support and test?

question.default_processing.statement: Which recommended setup provides first use without technical configuration: on-device processing, a managed service or another approach? Decide download, hardware, account and cost expectations; user-supplied API keys may remain an optional advanced route.

question.quality_budgets.statement: Fast model-dependent response is accepted; no universal seconds limit is selected. After representative model/hardware measurements, fix the Danish/English corpus, meaning/name/number quality criteria and cold/warm end-to-end latency budgets. This calibration is pending acceptance evidence, not a demand for an arbitrary upfront time limit.

question.activation.statement: Which activation styles and modifier-only shortcuts are required on each platform? What happens while busy?

question.delivery.statement: What destination confidence, clipboard restoration, verification and duplicate-prevention policy should insertion use?

question.data_lifecycle.statement: Resolved policy: keep text history until user deletion by default, optional chosen cleanup period, both text versions when processed, and no audio history. Successful audio is deleted; failed audio expires after at most 24 hours or earlier successful retry/manual deletion. Exact implementation of expiry/crash cleanup is refined under the specification question, not a new product-default decision. An optional history-off feature is not included by this resolution.

question.text_modes.statement: Resolved: direct transcription is default; optional AI cleanup/adjustment uses editable general or app-specific system prompts. AI-answer workflow remains deferred. Activation and preview are separately scoped in question.ai_activation.

question.file_scope.statement: Which containers, maximum duration/size, progress/resume semantics and export metadata must the file workflow support?

question.engine_scope.statement: The existing cloud-provider families, Ollama and custom OpenAI-compatible text endpoints are the baseline, captured in source.provider_inventory. Still evaluate compact local models/runtime choices and revalidate current provider model/protocol compatibility during implementation. Optional CLI text providers are included. Subscription speech capability is separately tracked in question.subscription_speech.

question.wake_viability.statement: Does hands-free activation justify its false-trigger rate, resource cost and ongoing microphone use?

question.migration_scope.statement: Resolved: empty profile; no import of existing Vara history, settings or credentials.

question.interaction_design.statement: Develop a coherent interaction/design proposal for the accepted dictation, per-app history and settings experience. Bring consequential product/design choices to the user; do not require a fine-grained UI questionnaire. File processing is deferred.

question.technology.statement: With Rust as the working implementation direction and all three desktop platforms targeted from the start, which UI toolkit, audio/media dependencies and OS adapters best satisfy the contracts? Their real crossplatform behavior must be verified in the agreed final phase.

question.release_distribution.statement: Which signing, distribution, update/recovery and sustainable maintenance arrangements are needed?

question.specification.statement: Before implementation, refine the chosen slice with complete types, external effects, risk/error coverage and resolved relevant questions; no contract sketch here claims readiness.

question.platform_envelope.statement: Within the accepted macOS/Windows/Linux first-release targets, which OS versions, CPU architectures, Linux distributions/desktop environments and integration fallbacks define the supported/tested envelope? Set this before final platform acceptance; it does not require early access to Windows/Linux. Include supported configurable shortcut forms, any modifier-only requirements and conflict/permission limitations; no universal key-support claim is implied.

question.cloud_access.statement: Resolved: cloud always uses personal provider API keys with easy in-app setup. No Vara-managed cloud/login/billing service in scope. Local is the key-free default; provider/model inclusion is addressed in question.engine_scope.

question.text_retention.statement: Should text history expire by default or only after manual deletion, with optional user-selected automatic cleanup?

question.text_versions.statement: When optional processing occurs, save both original and finished text and show the finished text first?

question.audio_policy.statement: Delete audio after successful transcription, temporarily retain failed captures for retry, and omit audio from history?

question.ai_activation.statement: Resolved: explicit per-app enablement automatically runs that originating app’s prompt; otherwise direct transcription is default. General prompt configuration does not imply global automatic processing. Transformed-output preview is separately scoped in question.ai_preview.

question.ai_preview.statement: Resolved: AI-processed text uses ordinary focus-safe delivery, automatic with unchanged original target and ready for manual insertion otherwise. No extra preview/approval step is required.

question.provider_baseline.statement: Use existing Vara provider families and own endpoints as the initial baseline with clear extensible contracts?

question.cli_routes.statement: Resolved: include Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI as optional text providers through genuine installed/authenticated tools. This is an explicit separate auth route from direct cloud API keys; actual processing locality remains enforced.

question.subscription_speech.statement: Which supported subscription/account-authenticated CLI speech routes can satisfy Vara’s STT contract? Research found documented Gemini audio+cached-headless capability, experimental local Codex realtime schemas, and Claude native dictation without an established external-audio/headless entry. Live entitlement, fidelity, latency and cancellation remain unverified; no route is promised as a release speech engine.
